56.title: Universal Unity
56.b0.ask: “How is a universe so varied, and at times so seemingly out of tune, held together as one in the one God?”
56.b2.p: In Paper 55 we saw how worlds settled in light and life move toward their completion. Now Paper 56 gathers all these stories together and speaks of the oneness running through the whole universe. Its opening words are short and clear: God is unity, and the universe of universes is one vast integrated mechanism absolutely controlled by one infinite mind (56:0.1).
56.b3.p: Because the perfect and the imperfect are truly interrelated, the finite evolutionary creature can ascend to Paradise in obedience to the command, “⟦Q 56:0.1|1:0.3|1:0.6⟧Be you perfect, even as I am perfect⟦/Q⟧” (56:0.1). To the limited minds of mortals the universe may look disordered and out of harmony, but those who see more widely better perceive the basic unity and single purpose beneath its diversity (56:0.2).
56.b4.p: How, then, do matter, mind, and spirit, personality and Deity, and truth, beauty, and goodness each become one?
56.b5.q: ⟦Q 56:9.14⟧God is all and in all, and no things or beings exist without him.⟦/Q⟧
56.b8.p: The material creation is not infinite, but it is perfectly co-ordinated. There are force, energy, and power, but all are one in origin. The seven superuniverses are seemingly dual and the central universe triune, but Paradise is of single constitution (56:1.1). The Unqualified Absolute upholds the physical universe, the Deity Absolute motivates the overcontrol of all material reality, and the Universal Absolute unifies the two in function (56:1.2).
56.b9.t: Of single constitution — the actual source of all material universes
56.b10.p: All gravity centers in the personal presence of the Paradise Father of pure energy and pure spirit (56:1.3). In the infinite nature of the Father there can be no duality of physical and spiritual reality; in him all things consist (56:1.4-1.5). But the moment we look away from that infinite level, we must postulate mind as the inevitable way of unifying these two seemingly divided manifestations (56:1.6).
56.b12.p: The Thought-Father finds spirit expression in the Word-Son and reaches out through Paradise into the material universes. What links the two is the mind ministry of the Infinite Spirit (56:2.1). Because the Father’s primal thought is eternalized in a twofold expression — the Isle of Paradise and the Eternal Son — the existence of the Infinite Spirit, the mind God, is inevitable (56:2.2).
56.b13.q: ⟦Q 56:2.2⟧Mind is the indispensable channel of communication between spiritual and material realities.⟦/Q⟧
56.b14.p: This infinite mind is ministered in time and space as the cosmic mind, reaching from the primitive ministry of the adjutant spirits up to the magnificent mind of a universe chief executive. Yet even the cosmic mind is unified under the Seven Master Spirits and, through the Supreme Mind, perfectly joined to the mind of the Infinite Spirit (56:2.3). Only through the ministry of mind can a material creature recognize the indwelling spirit (56:2.2).
56.b16.p: Just as mind gravity centers in the Infinite Spirit, spirit gravity centers in the personal presence of the Eternal Son (56:3.1). The spirit of Paradise is one, but in time and space it shows itself in several forms (56:3.2). In the local universe the Holy Spirit and the Spirit of Truth come forth from the headquarters of the Creator Sons and, together with the adjutant mind-spirits, reach down to the lower levels of material minds (56:3.3).
56.b17.t: The spirit personalities and emanations of the Son
The spirit personalities and influences of the Spirit and associated creations
The Father’s gift of the Thought Adjusters and other prepersonal spirit entities
56.b18.p: The mortal mind is created by the children of the Son and the Spirit, and when it fuses with the Father’s Adjuster, it shares in a threefold spirit endowment. These three expressions become perfectly unified in the finaliters (56:3.5). Spirit must always become threefold in expression and Trinity-unified in final realization (56:3.6).
56.b20.p: The Universal Father is a divinely unified personality, so his ascending children, led by the Thought Adjusters toward Paradise, will also be fully unified personalities before they reach Havona (56:4.1). Personality by nature reaches out to unify all its parts. Because mortal personality is a direct gift of the Father, it too has the power to unify the factors of a person’s being. This unifying power is a birthmark of its high source and evidence of its unbroken link with the Father through the personality circuit (56:4.2).
56.b21.p: Philosophically we may, and must, think of plural Deities and plural Trinities. But in the experience of worship, God is always one (56:4.5). Just as no child can have more than one father, to a personality God can never be plural (56:4.4).
56.b22.q: ⟦Q 56:4.4⟧To personality God cannot be plural. God is Father to each of his creatures, and it is literally impossible for any child to have more than one father.⟦/Q⟧
56.b24.p: There are three eternal personalizations of Deity — the Father, the Son, and the Spirit — but in the Paradise Trinity they are actually one Deity, undivided and indivisible (56:5.1). In the superuniverses today, the Supreme Creators form the first three levels of God the Sevenfold, and this whole domain is being co-ordinated in the evolving Supreme Being (56:5.3).
56.b25.t: First three levels of God the Sevenfold
The Creator Sons and Creative Spirits
56.b26.t: The evolving universes of time and space
56.b28.p: The spirit personality of the Supreme Being comes forth from the Paradise Deities, while the power of the Almighty Supreme rises up from the Creator divinities of the grand universe; the two are unified on the pilot world of the outer Havona circuit (56:6.2). Before the superuniverses were created, God the Supreme functioned only on spiritual levels, but the power of Supremacy grew as the universes evolved.
56.b29.p: On any level, God cannot exceed the conceptual capacity of the beings on that level. So mortal man begins with recognizing truth, appreciating beauty, and worshiping goodness, comes to know a God of love, and then moves step by step toward the comprehension of the Supreme (56:6.3). Ascenders grasp the power of the Almighty on the superuniverse capitals and the personality of the Supreme on the outer circuits of Havona, but actually finding the Supreme Being lies far in the future, even for the finaliters (56:6.4).
56.b31.p: Whenever a world, system, constellation, or universe reaches the height of its evolution, the function of Deity in that unit is enlarged, and the effects reach out to every other part of creation (56:7.1). As a local universe settles in light and life, God the Sevenfold becomes more and more clearly manifest (56:7.2).
56.b32.t: The Creator Son-Creative Spirit association is in control
The Son-Spirit liaison reaches full function
The second phase of God the Sevenfold becomes more active
Direct ministry of the Master Spirits; the revelation of God the Supreme begins
56.b33.p: Ascenders may experience the impersonal presence of the Deities long before they can know them as persons (56:7.4). And the authors honestly admit that they do not know what the Creators of God the Sevenfold will do in outer space once the grand universe is settled. They conjecture that the Michaels will serve in the outer universes, and they believe the perfected superuniverses will become part of the ascension path of beings from there (56:7.6-7.9).
56.b35.t: He is the unifier of time-space divinity, God the Sevenfold
He is the maximum of Deity that finite creatures can comprehend
He is man’s only avenue to fellowship with absonite mind, eternal spirit, and Paradise personality
56.b36.p: Finaliters are born in the local universes, nurtured in the superuniverses, and trained in the central universe; then they serve in other superuniverses one after another, adding experience to experience. In this way they come truly to know the Supreme Being, and they are destined to serve and reveal him in the outer universes of the future (56:8.2).
56.b37.p: All that the Father and his Sons do for us, we in turn have the chance to do for the Supreme Being. The Father does not need his sons to return to him what he gives, but they may pass it all on to their fellows and to the evolving Supreme Being (56:8.3). As Jesus said, the Son does what he sees the Father do; and we mortals too may soon begin to reveal the Supreme to our fellows (56:8.4).
56.b39.p: The Unqualified Absolute and the Deity Absolute are unified in the Universal Absolute. On subinfinite levels there are three Absolutes, but in infinity they appear to be one, just as the three persons of Paradise are one in the Trinity (56:9.1). Whether the Absolute came before the Trinity is the major philosophic question of the master universe, but the eternity of the Trinity rules out the idea that the Absolute is the ancestor of all things (56:9.2-9.4).
56.b40.p: In the end the creature mind returns to the Universal I AM, the Paradise Father, as the primal cause and source of both the Trinity and the Absolute (56:9.5). Whether we attain God the Sevenfold, comprehend God the Supreme, or find God the Ultimate, at the end of each adventure we will discover that on a new level we have rediscovered the same Father (56:9.10). The march of creation — force organizers mobilizing energy, Creator Sons organizing inhabited universes, creatures ascending to the Father — will keep widening without end (56:9.12-9.13).
56.b41.t: Mobilize energy to respond to the gravity pull of Paradise
Organize these forces into inhabited universes
Ascend to the Father to become like him
56.b43.p: On worlds settled in light and life, the chief pursuit of mortals is the comprehensible elements of Deity: truth, beauty, and goodness (56:10.2). Beauty is largely the unification of contrasts. The supreme beauty is the drama of man finding God and God finding man — the creature becoming perfect as the Creator is perfect. Materialism, atheism, is therefore the maximation of ugliness (56:10.3-10.4).
56.b44.t: Hunger for harmony and thirst for beauty
Love of the beautiful and appreciation of the artistry of all creation
Through truth, beauty leads to recognizing goodness — and on to God-consciousness
56.b45.t: Science and philosophy, the intellectual foundation of religion
The ministry of the Paradise Sons
Art, music, and the rhythms of experience
The reflection of Paradise in the material creation
The loving ministry of the personalities of the Infinite Spirit
56.b46.p: Only sin is isolated and resists gravity on the levels of mind and spirit. The universe is a whole; no one lives in isolation, and cosmic socialization is the highest form of personality unification (56:10.14). Love is the sum total of these three qualities, and advanced mortals know that love is the greatest thing in the universe — and that God is love (56:10.17, 10.20).
56.b47.q: ⟦Q 56:10.21⟧Love is the desire to do good to others.⟦/Q⟧
56.b49.p: Paper 56 shows the universe in many layers, but it tells us that all of them finally gather in the One. Matter is unified by Paradise gravity, mind by the Infinite Spirit, and spirit by the Eternal Son, and all of these become one in the personality of the Father. In the evolving universes this oneness is not a given fact but an achievement still being made, with the Supreme Being at the center of that unification. And our own personality is a piece of this unity. Just as the personality we received from the Father binds together body, mind, and spirit, so truth, beauty, and goodness become one in love — and that love shows itself in our lives as the simple desire to do good to others.
56.b50.t: All force and energy center in the presence of the Paradise Father
Mind is the indispensable channel between spirit and matter
Spirit is threefold in expression and one in realization
To personality, God can never be plural
A fact on Paradise, an achievement in the evolving universes
From truth, beauty, and goodness we move toward comprehending the Supreme
As the universe settles, God the Sevenfold is ever more clearly revealed
We pass on what we receive from the Father to our fellows and to the Supreme
At the end of every adventure we meet the same Father on a new level
The sum of the three values is love, and God is love
56.b52.box: The universe of universes is one in the one Father, and that oneness is completed within us as love.
57.title: The Origin of Urantia
57.b0.ask: “How did the long history of the universe, which began in one vast nebula, finally arrive at Urantia, the small planet we live on?”
57.b2.p: In Paper 56 we saw how the universe of universes is unified in one God. Now, beginning with Paper 57, we turn our eyes to the ground beneath our feet and ask how our own world was born within that unified universe. The story is drawn from the archives of Jerusem and is told by a Life Carrier, a member of the original Urantia Corps.
57.b3.p: The narrator tells us he will reckon time by our present calendar of 365¼ days to the year. Although exact dates are on record, he will not give them; he will use the nearest whole numbers instead. Every date is counted backward from the early decades of the twentieth century.
57.b4.p: So how did a whirl of space-energy, hundreds of billions of years ago, pass step by step into suns, then into planets, and at last into seas waiting for life?
57.b5.q: ⟦Q 57:8.26⟧These inland seas of olden times were truly the cradle of evolution.⟦/Q⟧
57.b8.p: Urantia came from our sun, and our sun is one of the many offspring of the Andronover nebula. That nebula itself took origin long, long ago in the universal force-charge of space in the superuniverse of Orvonton. The Primary Master Force Organizers of Paradise had long been in full control of those space-energies, and everything began with the report of a single inspector.
57.b9.t: Inspector number 811,307 reported that a sector in the eastern part of Orvonton was favorable for materialization
The Uversa Council of Equilibrium authorized the dispatch of a force organizer and staff
Andronover nebula number 876,926 was duly initiated
57.b10.p: To start the nebula turning, only the presence of the force organizer and the liaison staff was needed. Once the whirl began, they simply withdrew at right angles to the plane of the revolving disk, and from then on the inherent qualities of energy ensured an orderly evolution. At this point the story shifts to the work of the power directors and physical controllers of the superuniverse.
57.b12.p: All evolutionary material creations are born of circular, gaseous nebulae. As they grow older they usually become spiral, and they often end as clusters of stars or as enormous suns surrounded by planets. In this period Andronover was an ordinary primary nebula; astronomers in neighboring universes saw very little in it to attract their attention.
57.b13.t: Well established as one of the primary nebulae of Orvonton
Grown to gigantic size; additional physical controllers sent from nine surrounding creations
Height of energy mobilization; maximum mass reached — a vast circular gas cloud like a flattened spheroid
57.b15.p: Slowly the nebula began to take on a spiral form. It looked exactly like the spiral nebulae that astronomers today see through their telescopes. As it contracted, it spun faster, the grip of gravity weakened, and at last suns began to be thrown off into space one after another. This is how most of the suns of Orvonton were born.
57.b16.t: The first Andronover sun was born
The recaptive period began; Michael of Nebadon chose this nebula
Solar circuits well established; Michael’s staff arrived on Salvington
The first planets cooled enough for life implantation — the oldest inhabited worlds of Nebadon
Condensation tension at its peak; heat began to win over gravity, ending the secondary career
57.b17.p: Scarcely a million years after the recaptive period began, Michael chose this disintegrating nebula as the site of his adventure in universe building. The architectural worlds of Salvington and the constellation headquarters planets were begun almost at once. The evolution of the physical nebula and the building of the local universe went forward side by side.
57.b19.t: The second and last sun dispersion — ending as a globular cluster or a solitary sun
57.b20.p: Seventy-five billion years ago the first period of sun losses reached its height, and by the time it ended fifty billion years ago, 876,926 sun systems had been born. Ten billion years ago the quartan cycle began, and eight billion years ago a terrific terminal eruption broke out that lasted almost two billion years.
57.b21.p: Six billion years ago, as the terminal breakup ended, our sun was born — the fifty-sixth from the last of the second Andronover solar family. In all, 1,013,628 suns came from Andronover, and our sun’s number is 1,013,572. The great nebula is no more, yet its final nuclear remnant still burns with a reddish glow, giving light and heat to a family of one hundred and sixty-five worlds.
57.b22.h: 5. Origin of Monmatia—The Urantia Solar System
57.b23.p: Five billion years ago our sun was a comparatively isolated blazing orb and a variable star. Its surface heaved in great pulsations that took three and one-half days to complete a cycle, and this pulsing made it highly responsive to outside influences. Here begins the unique origin of Monmatia, our solar system; less than one per cent of the planetary systems of Orvonton have had a similar origin.
57.b24.p: Four and a half billion years ago the enormous Angona system, centered on a dark giant of space, drew near. Angona’s gravity broke off tongues of gas streaming from the sun, and at its closest approach it drew out a vast column of solar gases, pointed at both ends and bulging at the center. That column became the twelve planets. Yet although Angona drew this material out, it did not secure any of it for itself.
57.b25.t: The five inner and five outer planets
Jupiter and Saturn — for a short time they shone as secondary suns
The ejection from the opposite side
The meteors and space dust of the solar system
57.b26.p: This is why the planets do not travel in the plane of the sun’s equator but in the plane of the Angona extrusion. And three planets of the Angona system swung so near that they were torn loose and collided with the young system, bringing retrograde motion into it. Retrograde motion always results from the collision of space bodies of diverse origin.
57.b27.h: 6. The Solar System Stage—The Planet-Forming Era
57.b28.p: The planets nearest the sun were the first to have their spin slowed by tidal friction; this is why Mercury and the moon always turn the same face toward the larger body. When a small body comes too close to a larger one, gravity-tidal action tears it apart. Saturn’s rings are the fragments of a disrupted satellite, and the asteroids are what remains of the fifth planet, which long ago came too close to Jupiter and was shattered.
57.b29.t: What the solar system was like
The Jupiter and Saturn systems organized much as they are today
The cores of the other ten planets well formed — the era of planetary assembly
Functioning much as it does today; registered as Monmatia
Urantia about one tenth of its present mass
57.b30.p: All of this is the normal astronomic preparation an evolutionary world like Urantia passes through before the stage is set for the life adventures of time.
57.b31.h: 7. The Meteoric Era—The Volcanic Age—The Primitive Planetary Atmosphere
57.b32.p: In the early times, with no protective atmosphere, meteors crashed directly onto Urantia’s surface, and heavier elements such as iron gradually settled toward the center. As radioactive elements brought in by meteors were buried deeper and deeper, the inner heat grew and definite volcanic action began. The radium clock is our most reliable timepiece for estimating the planet’s age, but all such estimates are too short, because the radioactive materials we can examine came to the surface comparatively recently.
57.b33.t: Clearly outgrowing the moon; one fifth of its present size; able to hold a primitive atmosphere
Two thirds of its present size; volcanic action at its height — the volcanic age
57.b34.p: The primitive atmosphere held water vapor, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, and hydrogen chloride, but little or no free oxygen, because burning meteors and flowing lava kept using it up. When the air cooled, rain began to fall, and for thousands of years the earth lay wrapped in a blanket of steam; the sun never shone on its surface. Free oxygen gathered only much later, generated by the seaweeds and other plant life.
57.b35.h: 8. Crustal Stabilization—The Age of Earthquakes—The World Ocean and the First Continent
57.b36.p: One billion years ago is the date of the actual beginning of Urantia history. The planet had reached about its present size, and at this time it was placed on the registries of Nebadon under the name Urantia. As the crust cooled and the waters gathered, a world-wide ocean averaging over a mile deep covered the planet. This first ocean was not salty; it was practically fresh water.
57.b37.t: One great continent and one ocean, the Pacific; assigned to the system of Satania
The first scouting party from Jerusem (twenty-four members) arrived and found the planet suitable for a life experiment
The first real epoch of crustal stabilization began
The first great land epoch — one third of the surface was land, all in one continent
The first breaks in the continent, cracking north-and-south and east-and-west
Shallow seas and sheltered bays formed, suited to life
The continental seas spread and reached the saltiness life required
57.b38.p: On the scouting party’s report, Urantia was registered as a decimal planet and announced as the site of the Life Carriers’ sixtieth Satania experiment. The narrator adds that this small and insignificant sphere was destined to be the planet of Michael’s mortal bestowal, later known locally as the “⟦Q 57:8.6|20:6.6|119:8.8⟧world of the cross.⟦/Q⟧”
57.b39.q: ⟦Q 57:8.26⟧It was these seas and their successors that laid down the life records of Urantia, as subsequently discovered in well-preserved stone pages, volume upon volume, as era succeeded era and age grew upon age.⟦/Q⟧
57.b40.p: Mountains are not formed by the collapse of a cooling crust; they appear later through rain, gravity, and erosion. Even today Urantia averages fifteen earthquakes a day.
57.b42.p: Paper 57 tells a story spanning hundreds of billions of years as a calm chronicle. Force organizers set space-energy in motion; the Andronover nebula gave birth to suns; the passing Angona system drew out our solar system; and meteors, volcanoes, and rain shaped the earth. None of this was random upheaval. It was the normal preparation an evolutionary world goes through, and meanwhile Michael was building Nebadon on the site of the very same nebula. The history of the physical universe and the history of spiritual administration flow side by side until they meet at last in warm, shallow seas waiting for life. Those seas became the cradle of our life.
57.b43.t: Once the force organizers start the whirl, energy brings itself into order
A circular gaseous nebula grows to its maximum mass
The spiral nebula gives birth to suns, and Michael chooses it as the site of his universe
Our sun was born six billion years ago in the final breakup
5. Origin of Monmatia—The Urantia Solar System
The gas column drawn out by Angona became the twelve planets
6. The Solar System Stage—The Planet-Forming Era
The planets are assembled amid tidal forces and meteoric capture
7. The Meteoric Era—The Volcanic Age—The Primitive Planetary Atmosphere
The fiery earth cools and the rains begin
8. Crustal Stabilization—The Age of Earthquakes—The World Ocean and the First Continent
A fresh-water ocean and one continent prepare the cradle of life
57.b45.box: The long preparation of the universe was completed in seas ready to receive life, and those seas became the cradle of life on Urantia.
58.title: Life Establishment on Urantia
58.b0.ask: “When, where, and after what preparations did the Life Carriers plant the first life on Urantia, and how did that life spread?”
58.b2.p: In Paper 57 we followed the physical birth of Urantia — from nebula to sun, from sun to planet — up to the shallow seas waiting for life. Paper 58 now tells how life was actually planted in those seas. The narrator is a member of the Urantia Life Carrier Corps now resident on the planet.
58.b3.p: On most inhabited worlds life is placed according to established techniques, and the Life Carriers have little leeway. But about one world in ten is designated a decimal planet, where they may experiment in order to modify or improve the standard types of life. In all Satania there are only sixty-one life-modification planets like Urantia.
58.b4.p: What, then, did the Life Carriers wait for? Where did they plant life? And how is the history of that life recorded today in the rocks beneath our feet?
58.b5.q: ⟦Q 58:4.1⟧Urantia life is unique, original with the planet.⟦/Q⟧
58.b8.p: Six hundred million years ago a commission of Life Carriers from Jerusem began to study the physical conditions of Urantia, world number 606 of the Satania system. It was their six hundred and sixth life initiation in Satania and their sixtieth opportunity to modify the standard life designs. Life Carriers cannot start life until a planet is ripe for it, nor can they make life develop faster than the planet’s physical progress allows.
58.b9.p: They had planned a sodium chloride pattern of life, so they had to wait until the ocean was salty enough. Even today the blood that circulates in our bodies is a solution in all essentials like the salt water that bathed the first living cells. The commission returned to Jerusem to wait for the continent to break up further, opening more inland seas and sheltered bays.
58.b10.t: Waiting until it was sufficient for sodium chloride life
Many inland seas, shallow waters, and sheltered bays
Seas 500–600 feet deep; sunlight penetrating more than 600 feet
Rich in carbon — ideal for plants, but no animal could live
58.b12.p: The atmosphere lets through to the earth only about one two-billionth of the sun’s total light. A layer of ozone beginning about ten miles up would be only one tenth of an inch thick at surface conditions, yet it shields us from destructive ultraviolet rays. Were it a trifle thicker, it would also block the health-giving ultraviolet rays we need. At night the atmosphere acts like a blanket, holding in heat and making life possible.
58.b13.q: ⟦Q 58:2.4⟧Your pleasant life on Urantia is due to the "fortuitous" influence of more than two-score apparently accidental protective operations similar to the action of this unique ozone layer.⟦/Q⟧
58.b14.p: That is why the narrator calls unimaginative those mechanists who see material creation and human evolution as an accident. The Urantia midwayers have gathered over fifty thousand facts of physics and chemistry that, they say, demonstrate intelligent purpose in the material creation.
58.b15.t: A constant 65 to 70 degrees below zero F.
Temperature rises again, reaching 1200° F. at the auroral level
Two conducting regions in the superstratosphere
58.b16.p: The auroras are directly related to sunspots. Sunspots act like enormous magnets, hurling charged particles out to the earth’s outer atmosphere, where their ionizing effect produces the auroral displays. Even the compass needle turns slightly east at sunrise and slightly west near sunset, because sunlight ionizes the upper atmosphere.
58.b18.p: In early universe times space was strewn with vast hydrogen clouds, veritable cosmic chemical laboratories holding every phase of evolving energy and changing matter. The short-ray energy of space is four hundred times greater than all other forms of radiant energy in organized space.
58.b19.p: Yet none of this tremendous energy activity has the least influence on the germ plasm of living things. The life implanted by the Life Carriers is fully resistant to this whole flood of short space rays. Even so, these cosmic conditions too had to evolve to a favorable state before life could be established.
58.b21.p: The name Life Carriers should not mislead us. They brought no life to Urantia. All life here was formulated right here on the planet, and no other world in all Satania, even in all Nebadon, has life just like that of Urantia.
58.b22.p: Five hundred fifty million years ago the Life Carrier corps returned. In co-operation with spiritual powers and superphysical forces they organized the original life patterns and planted them in the waters. All planetary life down to the days of Caligastia came from these three identical and simultaneous marine-life implantations.
58.b24.p: The three implantations were made with foresight. Even after the continents drifted apart and great oceans lay between them, each great land mass would carry this life with it in its warm-water seas. By five hundred million years ago primitive marine plant life was well established, and the continents had begun their slow drift.
58.b26.p: The earth’s core became as dense and rigid as steel, and the temperature at its center is slightly above that of the sun’s surface. The outer crust, about forty miles thick, rests on a mobile sea of molten basalt. Without this cushion the more severe earthquakes would literally shake the world to pieces. Earthquakes are caused by the sliding and shifting of the solid crust, not by volcanoes.
58.b27.t: A little more than five and one-half times
58.b28.p: The sea bottoms are heavy basalt and the continents lighter granite, so the continents float above the ocean beds and slowly tend to creep into the oceans. The continental pressure at ocean-bottom level is about 20,000 pounds to the square inch, while the water pressure there is only about 5,000.
58.b30.p: Four hundred fifty million years ago the transition from plant to animal life took place in the shallow waters of sheltered tropic bays and lagoons. This development was all inherent in the original life patterns. The slime molds that survive today, hard to classify as either plant or animal, are its remaining witnesses.
58.b31.p: Yet there are no connecting links between the great divisions of the animal kingdom, nor between the highest prehuman animals and the dawn men. The so-called missing links will forever remain missing, because they never existed. New species do not arise from the slow accumulation of small variations; they appear suddenly as full-fledged new orders of life. This is nothing supernatural; it is wholly biologic and natural.
58.b32.t: Formed in response to the action of physical law
Bestowed by the adjutant mind-spirits according to brain capacity
58.b33.p: Mind is not a physical evolution, but it depends wholly on the brain capacity that evolution provides. All living things swing back and forth through endless adjustments; those that attain cosmic unity persist, and those that fall short cease to exist.
58.b35.p: The rocks of the life-dawn or Proterozoic era lie at or near the surface over about one eighth of today’s land, with an average thickness of about one and one-half miles. They yield fossils of algae, corallike plants, primitive Protozoa, and spongelike transition organisms. Where such fossils are absent, it does not mean life was absent elsewhere; life was sparse in those early times and spread only slowly.
58.b36.t: The primitive fossil-bearing layer comes to the surface
Lake Superior and the Grand Canyon
The easiest record to interpret, in several layers
The St. Croix valley of Wisconsin
127 successive lava flows, with 65 or 70 strata exposed
58.b37.p: In this era life spread throughout the waters of the world, and the floors of the shallow inland seas were overrun with luxuriant plant growth. The whole story is written in the vast stone book of the world, and its pages unfailingly tell the truth if we learn to read them.
58.b38.q: ⟦Q 58:7.12⟧It is literally true, as your poet has said, "The dust we tread upon was once alive."⟦/Q⟧
58.b40.p: Paper 58 shows that life was not a seed dropped by chance but was planted after long waiting and careful preparation. The Life Carriers waited for the sea to become salty enough and for bays and lagoons to form, and, foreseeing the breakup of the continent, they planted life in three places. More than two-score protective operations guarded that life, and it moved from plant to animal along the possibilities built into its original patterns. The story of that long struggle is still written in the rocks beneath our feet. The salt water in our blood remembers the first sea, and Urantia life is this planet’s own unique gift.
58.b41.t: Life was planted only after the sea had become salty enough
More than forty protective operations reveal intelligent purpose in creation
Implanted life was designed to withstand the space rays
Life planted in three places at once spread to every continent
The light continents float and move on a layer of molten lava
New species appear suddenly; the missing links never existed
The dust we tread upon was once alive
58.b43.box: Urantia life is a unique life, planted on this very planet after long preparation, and its history is written in the stone book.
59.title: The Marine-Life Era on Urantia
59.b0.ask: “During the two hundred and fifty million years in which the sea sheltered and raised life, through what stages did life prepare itself to step onto the land?”
59.b2.p: In Paper 58 we heard how the Life Carriers planted the first life in three seas 550 million years ago. Paper 59 now follows the long age in which that life grew and diversified in the waters. The narrator is a Life Carrier of Nebadon, one of the original corps assigned to Urantia.
59.b3.p: He divides the roughly one billion years of Urantia history into five major eras. The marine-life era covers two hundred and fifty million years, about one quarter of the planet’s history, and is divided into six long periods. As it opens, the sea bottoms and continental shelves are covered with prolific vegetation, and the stage is set for the opening chapters of the great “stone book.”
59.b4.p: How, then, did life advance from trilobites to fishes and frogs? And why did this era end in a time of biologic tribulation?
59.b5.q: ⟦Q 59:6.12⟧The sea mothered and nurtured the early life of the realm.⟦/Q⟧
59.b7.h: 1. Early Marine Life in the Shallow Seas—The Trilobite Age
59.b9.p: When this era opened, life was confined to the inland seas and the ocean shore line; no land organism had yet evolved. By 400 million years ago marine life was spread over the whole world, and vegetation for the first time crawled out onto the land. Then, suddenly and without gradation ancestry, the first multicellular animals appeared: the trilobites, which dominated the seas for ages.
59.b10.t: In shallow water where waves kept mud from settling
In deep water, containing trilobite shells
59.b11.p: The world climate was oceanic, and the warm Gulf Stream bathed the shores of Greenland, making that now ice-mantled continent a tropic paradise. The trilobites grew from two inches to one foot long and developed into carnivorous, herbivorous, omnivorous, and “mud eater” groups. Being the last multicelled animals able to live largely on inorganic matter explains their great increase and long survival. This fifty-million-year period is the Cambrian.
59.b12.h: 2. The First Continental Flood Stage—The Invertebrate-Animal Age
59.b13.p: The rising and sinking of the land in these times was gradual and undramatic. The Asiatic mother continent did not fully share the history of the other land masses, and in recent ages Asia has been the most stable of all.
59.b14.t: The great flood period began on all continents except central Asia
Another sinking — a great limestone age
A quiet time, broken by the great volcano of eastern Kentucky
The third major flood; eastern North America and western Europe deeply submerged
Mexico emerged, creating the Gulf Sea
59.b15.p: This was the great age of individual animal evolution. Marine animals developed until every type below the vertebrates appeared in the fossils, but there was still too much carbon dioxide in the air for land animals. Trilobites flourished in tens of thousands of patterns, and cephalopods, gastropods, bivalves, and brachiopods appeared much as they exist today. This period is the Ordovician.
59.b16.h: 3. The Second Great Flood Stage—The Coral Period—The Brachiopod Age
59.b17.p: Three hundred million years ago another great submergence began, and lime-shelled creatures built up the first widespread limestone layer, averaging about one thousand feet thick. By 290 million years ago the early mountain movements had begun, among them the Himalayas and the great Caledonian Mountains, and the deposits of this age hold much gas, oil, zinc, and lead.
59.b18.p: The trilobites rapidly declined, and the cephalopods, growing to fifteen feet long, appeared suddenly and became masters of the seas. The rocks laid down by the submergence of 280 million years ago are the Niagara limestone over which Niagara Falls now flows. Toward the close of this period the primitive water scorpions evolved, and soon after, suddenly, came the true scorpions — the first actual air breathers. These twenty-five million years are the Silurian.
59.b19.h: 4. The Great Land-Emergence Stage—The Vegetative Land-Life Period—The Age of Fishes
59.b20.p: In the long struggle between land and water, the time of land victory now arrives. The naked landscape becomes clothed with green, and the first magnificent forests soon appear. The age of 270 million years ago was one of the greatest land-emergence epochs in all world history.
59.b21.p: The greatest event of this age was the sudden appearance of the fishes. When the first vertebrates of the animal world came from the north 250 million years ago, their forerunners, modified arthropods, were quickly destroyed. Today’s sharks are survivors of these ancient fishes. On land the prolific fern family suddenly appeared and spread, and the forests of that day were silent forests; not even the rustle of a leaf was heard, for the trees had no leaves.
59.b22.t: One with a long body joining head and tail; a backboneless, jawless prefish
The fishes — appearing suddenly, while the forerunners were soon destroyed
59.b23.p: This age of fishes, lasting almost fifty million years, is the Devonian.
59.b24.h: 5. The Crustal-Shifting Stage—The Fern-Forest Carboniferous Period—The Age of Frogs
59.b25.p: The appearance of fish marks the apex of marine-life evolution; from here on, the evolution of land life becomes more and more important. When the seas were at their height, the first land animals suddenly appeared: air-breathing amphibians that developed from arthropods whose swim bladders had evolved into lungs. Snails, scorpions, and frogs crawled out of the sea onto the land, and frogs still lay their eggs in water.
59.b26.p: Soon the insects appeared and spread, with dragon flies measuring thirty inches across. From 200 million years ago coal formation went on for a little over twenty-five million years. Coal is the remains of rank swamp vegetation preserved by water and changed by pressure; tree roots still standing in the clay beneath the coal beds show that it formed exactly where it is found.
59.b27.t: Times of sinking and rising shown by the coal beds
59.b28.p: The Carboniferous period closed 180 million years ago, and as the land rose, the mild marine climate began to give way to a more variable continental climate. The life features of the coal age were ferns and frogs.
59.b29.h: 6. The Climatic Transition Stage—The Seed-Plant Period—The Age of Biologic Tribulation
59.b30.p: This was an age of great life impoverishment. At the close of the marine-life era there were more than one hundred thousand species on earth; at the close of this transition fewer than five hundred had survived. The cause was not catastrophe but a combination of commonplace influences: shrinking seas and rising land. The mild marine climate disappeared, and two new climatic factors appeared — glaciation and aridity.
59.b31.t: The seed plants first appeared, providing better food
Resting stages evolved to survive winter and drought
They declined, but in Africa took the first step toward the reptiles
They took refuge in three retreats: the Gulf of Mexico, the Ganges Bay, and the Sicilian Bay
59.b32.p: By 160 million years ago the land was covered with vegetation and the atmosphere had become ideal for animal breathing. The trials of this age eliminated every form of life except those with survival value, which were therefore fit to be the ancestors of the faster-developing life of the ages to come. With the end of this Permian period the Paleozoic era also closes.
59.b33.q: ⟦Q 59:6.12⟧The vast oceanic nursery of life on Urantia has served its purpose.⟦/Q⟧
59.b35.p: Paper 59 tells the story of two hundred and fifty million years of sea life in six periods. The land sank and rose again and again, and each time a new page was laid down in the rocks. Meanwhile the trilobites ruled the seas, the cephalopods followed, the fishes opened the door to the vertebrates, and the frogs at last climbed onto the land. New forms of life usually appeared suddenly, and at the end of the era a harsh trial left only the life with survival value. The sea mothered and nurtured life until the land was ready to receive it; now, its work done, it hands the second stage of evolution over to the land.
59.b36.t: 1. Early Marine Life in the Shallow Seas—The Trilobite Age
The trilobites, the first multicellular animals, appear suddenly and rule the seas
2. The First Continental Flood Stage—The Invertebrate-Animal Age
Every type of marine animal below the vertebrates develops
3. The Second Great Flood Stage—The Coral Period—The Brachiopod Age
The cephalopods master the seas and the first air breathers appear
4. The Great Land-Emergence Stage—The Vegetative Land-Life Period—The Age of Fishes
The fishes, the first vertebrates, and the silent forests appear
5. The Crustal-Shifting Stage—The Fern-Forest Carboniferous Period—The Age of Frogs
Frogs climb onto the land and coal is laid down
6. The Climatic Transition Stage—The Seed-Plant Period—The Age of Biologic Tribulation
A harsh trial leaves only life with survival value
59.b38.box: The sea has fulfilled its purpose as the cradle of life, and the life that survived its trials now moves onto the land.
60.title: Urantia During the Early Land-Life Era
60.b0.ask: “Why did the giant dinosaurs disappear, and how did the hundred million years of reptile rule open a path of evolution in which brains, not bodies, would grow?”
60.b2.p: In Paper 59 we saw the sea shelter and raise life for two hundred and fifty million years and then, after a harsh trial, hand its role over to the land. Paper 60 continues with the hundred million years in which land life ruled — the Mesozoic. The narrator is a Life Carrier of Nebadon now functioning on Urantia.
60.b3.p: The era of exclusive marine life has ended. Rising land, a cooling crust and cooling oceans, and shrinking, deepening seas greatly changed the climate everywhere far from the equator. The frogs, masters of the previous age, survived only in greatly reduced numbers, and even the spore-bearing plants were nearly extinct.
60.b4.p: On this new stage, how did the reptiles rise and decline? And meanwhile, how did flowers, birds, and mountains prepare the world we know today?
60.b5.q: ⟦Q 60:2.14⟧Henceforth, evolution will follow the growth of brains, not physical bulk, and the development of brains will characterize each succeeding epoch of animal evolution and planetary progress.⟦/Q⟧
60.b8.p: The gypsum and red layers in the deposits of this period show that the climate was arid. Fossils are few, but many sandstone footprints of land reptiles remain, and land-animal life continued only in certain parts of Africa. The early land-life periods began 150 million years ago. Life did not fare well, but it did better than at the hostile close of the marine-life era.
60.b9.p: Then, 140 million years ago, the reptiles appeared suddenly in full-fledged form. They soon gave rise to crocodiles, scaled reptiles, sea serpents, and flying reptiles, while their transition ancestors quickly disappeared. The dinosaurs soon became the monarchs of the age. They are set apart from all other animals by their small brains — less than one pound of brain controlling bodies that later weighed as much as forty tons.
60.b10.t: Smaller and carnivorous; walked kangaroolike on their hind legs; hollow, birdlike bones
Walked on all fours; one branch developed protective armor
60.b11.p: Several million years later the first mammals appeared, but they were nonplacental, proved a speedy failure, and none survived. In the seas the beautiful ammonites flourished. This twenty-five-million-year period is the Triassic.
60.b13.p: The great event of the period that began 120 million years ago was the evolution and decline of the dinosaurs. They evolved in every size, from species less than two feet long up to huge plant-eaters seventy-five feet long. But as they grew larger they became less active and strong. They needed so much food that they literally starved to death; they lacked the intelligence to cope with the situation.
60.b14.t: Two species that took to the water (sea serpents, ichthyosaurs)
A backward step — fifty feet long with brains under two ounces; they perished
They always returned to the land to lay their eggs
A line that did not survive and was not ancestral to the birds; they perished
60.b15.p: Some species progress, some strains stand still, and others slide backward to a former state. That is what happened to the sea serpents that forsook the land. In this period the turtles also first appeared in North America, their ancestors having come over from Asia by the northern land bridge, and in the lithographic stone of southern Germany the delicate wings of insects were preserved as of but yesterday.
60.b16.q: ⟦Q 60:2.14⟧The dinosaurs, for all their enormous mass, were all but brainless animals, lacking the intelligence to provide sufficient food to nourish such enormous bodies.⟦/Q⟧
60.b17.p: This period of nearly twenty-five million years, which saw the height of the reptiles and the beginning of their decline, is the Jurassic.
60.b18.h: 3. The Cretaceous Stage—The Flowering-Plant Period—The Age of Birds
60.b19.p: The Cretaceous period takes its name from the chalk-making foraminifers of its seas. In this period reptile dominance nears its end, flowering plants and birds appear, and the drift of the continents comes to a stop. As the westward-drifting continents met the deep floor of the Pacific, the vast north-south mountain range from Alaska to Cape Horn began to rise. The age of modern mountain building had opened.
60.b20.t: The angiosperms suddenly appeared and spread over the continents
The Bering Strait closed, making Atlantic and Pacific marine life alike
Continental drift halted; the circumpacific uplift — the greatest surface distortion since life appeared
The greatest elevation of the Rocky Mountains
One of the greatest lava flows in the world’s history
The first true birds, ancestors of all bird life, suddenly appeared
60.b21.p: Many modern trees — beech, oak, maple, and others — appeared at this time, along with fruits, grasses, and cereals. These seed-bearing grasses and trees were to the plant world what the ancestors of man were to the animal world; in evolutionary importance they were second only to the appearance of man himself.
60.b22.t: Too little brain; they became extinct
Second: the wading and swimming prebirds and the flying dinosaurs
No success in the air; short-lived
Third: the true birds, small and pigeonlike
Sprang directly from the reptiles and became the ancestors of all birds
60.b23.h: 4. The End of the Chalk Period
60.b24.p: The end of the Cretaceous period marks the end of the great sea invasions of the continents. North America had just twenty-four great inundations. Land and sea have alternated in dominance in million-year cycles, and this rhythm will go on, but with diminishing frequency and extent.
60.b25.p: The chief factor in fixing the location of a mountain range is not the pressure of the continents but a pre-existent lowland, or trough, filled with lighter deposits. When the crust is under pressure, these lighter areas are the first to crumple, fold, and rise.
60.b26.t: The older east-west systems of Asia, Greenland, and northern Europe
The circumpacific group and the second European east-west system, born about the same time
The Rocky Mountain system — raised again after erosion and carved into shape
60.b27.p: By the end of this period the fern forests had been largely replaced by modern trees such as the gigantic redwoods. The placental mammal had not yet evolved, but the stage was fully set for the ancestors of the mammals to appear in the next age. The fifty-million-year Cretaceous closes the hundred-million-year Mesozoic era.
60.b29.p: Paper 60 shows how the age of great bodies came to an end. The reptiles appeared suddenly and took over land, sea, and even sky, but without brains to match their bodies they could not feed themselves, and they disappeared. The lines that returned to the sea went backward, and two attempts at flight failed. Yet meanwhile flowering plants and seed-bearing grasses covered the world, the true birds appeared, and as the continents stopped drifting, today’s mountains rose. The lesson of this long age is clear: from now on evolution moves forward by the growth of brains, not the size of bodies, and at the end of that road stands man.
60.b30.t: The reptiles appear suddenly in full form, and the dinosaurs become monarchs
Huge bodies without intelligence cannot feed themselves and vanish
3. The Cretaceous Stage—The Flowering-Plant Period—The Age of Birds
Flowering plants and true birds appear, and the mountains rise
4. The End of the Chalk Period
The sea invasions end and the stage is set for the mammals
60.b32.box: The age of bulk has ended, and evolution now moves toward man by the growth of brains.
61.title: The Mammalian Era on Urantia
61.b0.ask: “How did the mammals, which care for their young and use their brains, take over the world, and how was man born in the frozen ice age?”
61.b2.p: In Paper 60 we saw the age of huge, unintelligent dinosaurs come to an end and evolution begin to follow the growth of brains. Paper 61 now takes up the age of the mammals that walked that road. It runs from the appearance of placental mammals to the end of the ice age, a little less than fifty million years. The account was sponsored by a resident Life Carrier.
61.b3.p: During this Cenozoic age the world was a lovely landscape of rolling hills, broad valleys, wide rivers, and great forests. The trees swarmed with birds, and the whole world was an animal paradise. The deposits of its five periods hold the fossil records of the successive mammalian dynasties, leading right up to the actual appearance of man himself.
61.b4.p: What advantages, then, let the mammals take over the world? And how did the ice age that came at the end fit together with the birth of man?
61.b5.q: ⟦Q 61:2.5⟧Brains and agility had replaced armor and size in the progress of animal survival.⟦/Q⟧
61.b7.h: 1. The New Continental Land Stage—The Age of Early Mammals
61.b8.p: Fifty million years ago the placental mammals suddenly appeared in North America — the most important evolutionary development up to that time. Their father was a small, highly active, carnivorous, springing type of dinosaur that had survived the dinosaur decline. In these primitive mammals the basic mammalian instincts began to show themselves.
61.b9.t: Bring forth relatively mature and well-developed offspring
Nourish, nurture, and protect their offspring with affectionate regard
Employ their superior brain power in self-perpetuation
Use increased agility to escape from enemies
Apply superior intelligence to adjusting and adapting to their surroundings
61.b10.p: Forty-five million years ago small horses, rhinoceroses, tapirs, primitive pigs, lemurs, and monkeylike animals lived in the forests, and an ostrichlike bird ten feet tall was the ancestor of the later gigantic passenger birds that once carried human beings through the air. The mammals of this time were all covered with hair and had large brains for their size, but no modern forms yet existed. This period is called the Eocene.
61.b11.h: 2. The Recent Flood Stage—The Age of Advanced Mammals
61.b12.p: Thirty-five million years ago the placental mammals began their world domination. Over one hundred species of the more primitive mammals died out, and even the mammals of large size and small brain soon perished. As the dinosaurs declined, the mammals took over the earth and completely destroyed what remained of their reptilian ancestors. The only survivors of the early reptiles are the turtles, snakes, and crocodiles, along with the venerable frog.
61.b13.p: Thirty million years ago modern types of mammals began to appear. From the mountain-dwelling mammals came the hoofed grazers of the plains, and camels and llamas had their origin in North America. In western North America the early ancestors of the line from which the true lemurs later sprang first appeared. And just as the serpents once did, a whole tribe of mammals left the land for the sea, becoming the whales, dolphins, seals, and sea lions. This ten-million-year period is the Oligocene.
61.b14.h: 3. The Modern Mountain Stage—Age of the Elephant and the Horse
61.b15.p: Twenty million years ago was indeed the golden age of mammals. Over the Bering Strait land bridge, mastodons and many members of the cat family came from Asia into North America, and deer and other ruminants filled the plains. For once the world was ruled by a huge animal with a brain large enough to match its body — the elephant.
61.b16.t: A large body, a large, superior brain, and emotional control — yet too big to be agile
Second only to the elephant in brain quality — but unable to overcome its urge to flee when afraid
The only being who surpasses the elephant in intelligence and adaptation
61.b17.p: The narrator notes that we are entering the so-called “horseless age,” and he urges us to pause and ponder what this animal meant to our ancestors, who used it for food, for travel, and later in agriculture and war. In central Asia the true types of the monkey and the gorilla evolved, but neither belongs to the line that later became the ancestors of the human race. This period is the Miocene.
61.b18.h: 4. The Recent Continental-Elevation Stage—The Last Great Mammalian Migration
61.b19.p: In this period just before the ice age, mountain ranges were born and rivers changed their courses, and Mounts Shasta, Hood, and Rainier began their careers as mountains. For a short time all the land of the world except Australia was joined again, and the last great world-wide animal migration took place.
61.b20.t: Horses (in their present form by 5 million years ago)
From North America to all the world
61.b21.p: As the climate cooled, the northern land bridges went down and the link between Africa and South America finally submerged. From then on the Eastern and Western Hemispheres each developed their own distinct types of life. By the close of this Pliocene period of almost ten million years, the ancestor of man had still not appeared.
61.b23.p: The lands of northeastern North America and northern Europe rose high, ocean currents and seasonal winds shifted, and snow fell almost constantly on the northern highlands. It piled up to a depth of 20,000 feet and turned into solid but creeping ice. The great ice sheets lay on these elevated highlands, not in the mountain regions where they are found today.
61.b25.p: The northern regions experienced six distinct ice invasions. Two million years ago the first glacier advanced south as far as Kansas, and 1,500,000 years ago the second invasion began. Early in the ice age North America teemed with mastodons, woolly mammoths, saber-toothed tigers, and many other animals, but as the cold increased most of them disappeared. The glaciers were, after all, local phenomena; away from the ice, life changed little.
61.b26.h: 6. Primitive Man in the Ice Age
61.b27.p: The great event of the glacial period was the evolution of primitive man. Slightly to the west of India, on land now under water, the dawn mammals suddenly appeared among the descendants of the older North American lemur types. The road to man ran through a series of sudden mutations.
61.b28.t: Walked mostly on their hind legs; large brains for their size
Suddenly differentiated in the seventieth generation; nearly twice the size, with more brain power
Appeared suddenly as the third vital mutation
One million years ago — the actual ancestors of mankind
61.b29.p: At the same time a backward development in the mid-mammal stock gave rise to the simian ancestry. From that day on the human branch went forward, while the simian tribes stood still or slid backward. One million years ago Urantia was registered as an inhabited world.
61.b30.q: ⟦Q 61:6.3⟧Your early ancestors were born and bred in a stimulating, invigorating, and difficult environment.⟦/Q⟧
61.b31.p: This happened at about the time the third glacial advance began. The Eskimos, the only survivors of these aborigines, still prefer to live in the frigid north. During the interglacial epochs human beings spread westward around the Mediterranean into Europe, but they did not reach the Western Hemisphere until near the close of the ice age.
61.b33.p: The glaciers left marks unlike those of any other natural process — moraines, drumlins, and distinctive boulders. And the advances of the ice can be dated alongside the history of mankind.
61.b34.t: The ice and the human story
The fourth ice sheet pushed the Mississippi River west
The fifth advance — the six colored races appeared, and the Planetary Prince arrived
The sixth and last glaciation began — the largest invasion in North America
The last glacier reached its farthest southern points
The Great Lakes began to empty out by way of Niagara
The great ice age ended except in the polar regions; the Adamic dispensation began
61.b35.p: The retreat of the last glacier produced the Great Lakes of North America, and as long as the polar regions remain covered with ice, another glacial age is hardly possible. The harsh ice age destroyed and sifted many species, and arctic plants and animals that climbed mountain peaks to escape the ice are still found high on the Alps and the Appalachians. This ice age of over two million years is the Pleistocene.
61.b37.p: Paper 61 carries the fifty-million-year story of the mammals up to the birth of man. The mammals won the world not by armor or size but by caring for their young, and by brains and agility. The elephant and the horse showed the power of those brains, and after the last great migration the continents each raised their own life. Then, in the harshest time, as the world was being covered with ice, two primitive human beings were born at the end of a series of sudden mutations. Our ancestors grew up not in a comfortable paradise but in a stimulating and difficult environment, and the timeline of the ice age runs alongside the human story — the six colored races, the Planetary Prince, the Lucifer rebellion, and the arrival of Adam.
61.b38.t: 1. The New Continental Land Stage—The Age of Early Mammals
Placental mammals that care for their young and use their brains suddenly appear
2. The Recent Flood Stage—The Age of Advanced Mammals
Brains and agility replace armor and size
3. The Modern Mountain Stage—Age of the Elephant and the Horse
The elephant, with a brain to match its body, rules the world
4. The Recent Continental-Elevation Stage—The Last Great Mammalian Migration
After the last great migration the two hemispheres raise their own life
Snow on the northern highlands brings six ice invasions
6. Primitive Man in the Ice Age
One million years ago two primitive human beings were born in a harsh environment
The dates of the glaciers match the great events of human history
61.b40.box: At the end of the mammals’ road, won by brains and by care for their young, man was born in the harsh environment of the ice age.
62.title: The Dawn Races of Early Man
62.b0.ask: “How did the first human beings, able to worship and to choose, come from a small line of lemurlike creatures?”
62.b2.p: In Paper 61 we watched the continents, the climate, and animal life being prepared, through the age of mammals, as a stage to receive man. Paper 62 now tells how man at last steps onto that stage. About one million years ago the immediate ancestors of mankind appeared by three successive and sudden mutations from early stock of the lemur type of placental mammal.
62.b3.p: The main strain of this stock came from the western, or American, group of the life plasm, but it was reinforced by contributions from the central life implantation evolved in Africa. The eastern life group contributed little or nothing to the human species. The paper is told by a Life Carrier of Nebadon resident on Urantia, who watched these events himself.
62.b4.p: What, then, was the road from the dawn mammals through the mid-mammals and the Primates to the first human beings? And when did the universe recognize this planet as a world inhabited by man?
62.b5.q: ⟦Q 62:7.3⟧This is the first decision of mind—the human type of mind—on Urantia and automatically establishes the circuit of communication⟦/Q⟧
62.b8.p: The early lemurs that became the ancestors of the human species were not directly related to the gibbons and apes then living in Eurasia and northern Africa. Nor were they descended from the modern lemur; both sprang from a common ancestor long since extinct.
62.b9.p: Several million years ago the North American lemurs crossed the Bering land bridge and slowly made their way southwest along the Asiatic coast. They reached a pleasant region to the west of India, joined there with other favorable strains, and so established the ancestry of the human race. Later, as the coast sank, this Mesopotamian or Persian peninsula became an isolated paradise with no way in or out except to the north. From it sprang two great groups: the simian tribes of modern times and the human species.
62.b10.t: They crossed westward and moved along the Asiatic coast
Joined with favorable strains, establishing the human ancestry
Isolated by the sinking coast, it became a sheltered refuge
62.b12.p: A little more than one million years ago the Mesopotamian dawn mammals suddenly appeared. They were hairy, agile creatures almost three feet tall, able to stand erect with ease; they chattered like monkeys but, unlike the simian tribes, they ate flesh. They had a primitive opposable thumb and a grasping big toe. From here on the prehuman line developed the thumb and gradually lost the grasping power of the great toe, while the later apes did the opposite.
62.b13.p: They had the largest brains for their size of any animal that had yet existed, and they already showed many of the emotions of later primitive man. Keenly aware of the dangers of the forest, they built shelters high in the treetops; the fear tendencies of mankind date from these days. Superior groups made war on inferior neighbors, so that by selective survival the species steadily improved, and just seventy generations later the next step suddenly branched off.
62.b14.t: Almost three feet tall; hairy and agile
Full grown at three or four; a life span of about twenty years
Curiosity, elation at success, family tenderness, self-abasement bordering on shame
Touchingly loyal, but choosing new partners if separated
Strong fear, tribal spirit, and pugnacity
62.b16.p: In the treetop home of a superior pair of dawn mammals, twins were born, a male and a female. They grew to a little over four feet, with longer legs and shorter arms, almost perfectly opposable thumbs, and feet suited to walking upright. Recognized early as heads of the tribe, this brother and sister introduced a primitive social organization and a crude division of labor. They mated and had twenty-one children, who formed the nucleus of the mid-mammals.
62.b17.p: After relentless war this new group wiped out the ancestral race entirely and dominated the region for almost fifteen thousand years. They were the first mammals to show disgust, to hoard food and pebbles, and to build shelters both in the treetops and underground. Yet through internal battles they came close to extinction, until only one group of fewer than one hundred remained.
62.b18.q: ⟦Q 62:3.9⟧Had the ancestral frog of all humanity jumped two inches less on a certain occasion, the whole course of evolution would have been markedly changed.⟦/Q⟧
62.b19.p: The closest call of all came when lightning struck the tree where the future mother of the Primates twins was sleeping. This couple survived, moved about two miles away with more than half the tribe, built new homes, and there gave birth to the first Primates twins. At the same time a mentally and physically inferior couple also had twins, who became the founders of the modern simian tribes. Man and the apes came from the same tribe, but not from the same parents.
62.b20.t: Twins born at the same time
Children of the two leading members — the line continued through the Primates to man
Concerned only with food, refusing flesh — ancestors of the monkey, baboon, chimpanzee, and gorilla
62.b22.p: The Primates twins had even less hair than their parents, stood erect from the beginning, and grew to over five feet. They learned to communicate with each other by signs and sounds, but they could never make their people understand these new symbols. At about fourteen they fled west to found a new species, very properly called the Primates, since they were the direct animal ancestors of the human family.
62.b23.p: The skeletons of the Primates were very much like those of primitive man, and their hands and feet had fully developed human form. Yet they were still greatly ruled by fear, slept in the treetops at night, and did not yet have minds that could truly be called human. About twenty-one thousand years after the dawn mammals appeared, after almost nine hundred generations, the Primates suddenly gave birth to the first two true human beings.
62.b26.p: Counting back from the year A.D. 1934, the first two human beings were born just 993,419 years ago. They had perfect human thumbs and feet like ours, with no grasping function of the big toe at all. When they climbed a tree, they went up the trunk like a bear rather than swinging up by the branches.
62.b27.p: The most remarkable advance was in their emotions. A worshipful group of feelings — awe, reverence, humility, and even a primitive form of gratitude — suddenly appeared, and fear joined with ignorance of nature was about to give birth to primitive religion. Higher sentiments such as pity, shame, love and hate, and jealousy were also present in rudimentary form.
62.b28.t: Admiration for objects and other beings; considerable vanity
Awe, reverence, humility, a primitive gratitude
Pity, shame, reproach; love, hate, and revenge; jealousy
62.b29.p: By the age of ten the twins had worked out a language of almost half a hundred ideas. When they were about nine, they went down the river one bright day and agreed to live with and for each other, and they later decided to journey north. The Life Carriers could not control their minds, but within the permitted limits they led them north to a secluded region, away from their inferior relatives. Shortly before they left, their mother gave her life defending them from a gibbon raid, and their father, left behind, died heartbroken.
62.b31.p: The Life Carriers followed the twins’ mental growth by watching the work of the seven adjutant mind-spirits. Through the long ages of evolution these mind ministers had steadily widened their contact with ever-larger animal brains. From the dawn mammals through the Primates, only the first five had functioned; the two highest had never yet been able to act.
62.b32.t: When and how it first appeared
In the instinctive and reflex behavior of primordial animals
Spontaneous association of ideas in higher types
Clearly seen after the mammals appeared
The herd instinct and early social development of higher mammals
When the twins were about ten — first the girl, soon after the boy
About a year later, at the decision to journey north
62.b33.p: When the spirit of worship touched first the mind of the girl twin and soon after that of the boy, the Life Carriers knew that something close to human mind was nearing completion. About a year later, when the twins resolved by meditative thought and purposeful decision to leave and go north, the spirit of wisdom began to function, and the two were recognized as having human minds.
62.b35.p: At noon on the day after the twins ran away, the first test flash of the universe circuit signals occurred at the planet’s reception-focus, and on the third day the archangel of initial planetary circuit establishment arrived. The first message from Salvington declared that the twins’ purposeful decision to flee northward was the first decision of the human type of mind on Urantia, and that this very decision had automatically opened the circuit of communication.
62.b36.t: Announced and celebrated the appearance of mind of will dignity
Instructed the Life Carriers not to interfere with the pattern of life
Accepted the Life Carriers’ work and gave them leave to return
62.b37.p: This formally ended the Life Carriers’ agelong supervision of the planet. Now that will — the power of choosing to worship and to ascend — had appeared, their work was finished. Because Urantia is a life-modification world, two senior Life Carriers and twelve assistants were allowed to remain, and the narrator was one of them. Urantia was formally recognized as a planet of human habitation just 993,408 years before A.D. 1934.
62.b38.q: ⟦Q 62:7.7⟧Biologic evolution had once again achieved the human levels of will dignity; man had arrived on planet 606 of Satania.⟦/Q⟧
62.b40.p: Paper 62 does not leave the origin of man as a list of chance events. A thin line of descent, nearly cut off again and again by lightning, war, and hunger, ran from the dawn mammals through the mid-mammals and the Primates, and at its end two twins were born. Yet what made them truly human was not only the shape of their bodies. The spirits of worship and wisdom touched their minds, and the two children, thinking for themselves, decided to go north together. That first act of will opened the universe circuits, and Urantia was recognized as a world inhabited by man. Our humanity began, in the end, with a mind that worships and chooses.
62.b41.t: Lemurs from America established the human line on an isolated peninsula
With the largest brains for their size came the beginning of human fear
Two pairs of twins from the same tribe divided into man and the apes
Man’s direct animal ancestors produced the first humans after nine hundred generations
Twins with worshipful feelings chose for themselves to go north
The human mind was completed as the spirits of worship and wisdom made contact
The first act of will opened the universe circuits, and Urantia was recognized
62.b43.box: Man was born with a mind that worships and chooses for itself, and its first decision joined Urantia to the universe.
63.title: The First Human Family
63.b0.ask: “How did Andon and Fonta, the parents of all mankind, live and die, and what did they leave to their descendants?”
63.b2.p: In Paper 62 we saw the first human twins born of the Primates and decide for themselves to go north. Paper 63 now enters into the lives of those twins. Urantia was registered as an inhabited world when the two were eleven years old, before they had become parents of the second generation.
63.b3.p: On that occasion the archangel’s message from Salvington named the parents of the new race Andon and Fonta and prayed that they might soon receive the gift of the spirit of the Universal Father. The names mean the first Fatherlike and the first Sonlike creatures to show a hunger for human perfection. But the two never knew these names; they called each other Sonta-an, “⟦Q 63:0.3⟧loved by mother,⟦/Q⟧” and Sonta-en, “⟦Q 63:0.3⟧loved by father.⟦/Q⟧”
63.b4.p: How, then, did this first couple live? Where did their family and clans spread? And what became of the two after death?
63.b5.q: ⟦Q 63:7.4⟧The story of the evolution, life struggles, death, and eternal survival of the unique parents of all mankind.⟦/Q⟧
63.b8.p: In many ways Andon and Fonta were the most remarkable pair of human beings who ever lived on earth. These actual parents of all mankind were superior to many of their descendants and radically different from all their ancestors. Their own parents belonged to the more intelligent part of their tribe, the group that first learned to throw stones and fight with clubs.
63.b9.p: Andon tied a sharp flint to the end of a club with animal tendons, and on no fewer than a dozen occasions this weapon saved his own life and his sister’s. Their decision to leave the Primates tribes shows a quality of mind far above that of their animal kin. Their vague feeling of being more than mere animals came from the possession of personality and was heightened by the indwelling Thought Adjusters.
63.b11.p: Even after deciding to leave, the twins were afraid — afraid of displeasing their father and family, and afraid of being killed by jealous relatives. One night, awakened by a violent storm, they held each other close and made their final decision. Though they dreaded the ground at night, they set out shortly before nightfall to avoid pursuit and reached their prepared hiding place shortly after midnight.
63.b12.p: On the way Andon saw sparks fly from flint and conceived the idea of making fire. As autumn deepened and the nights grew cold, the couple tried every day for two months to light a fire, until Fonta brought down a dry, abandoned bird’s nest and the spark burst into flame. Their ancestors had often kept alive fires lit by lightning, but no creature had ever before been able to start a fire at will.
63.b13.t: Andon saw sparks fly while chipping flint
Autumn deepened and the nights grew cold
For two months they failed every day to set wood alight
Fonta used a dry bird’s nest as tinder
They could defy the climate, free of their animal relatives in the south
63.b15.p: Almost two years after leaving home, their first child, Sontad, was born. Sontad was the first creature on Urantia to be wrapped in protective coverings at birth, and with him appeared the instinct to care for helpless infants. Andon and Fonta had nineteen children and lived to see almost half a hundred grandchildren and six great-grandchildren. They made their home in rock shelters, or semicaves, joined by hallways dug in the soft limestone.
63.b16.p: The early Andonites had a strong clannish spirit; they hunted together and never strayed far from home. This sense of close kinship came from the enhanced ministry of the adjutant spirits. Andon and Fonta were killed together at forty-two by a falling rock during an earthquake, and Sontad, despite an injured foot, took the lead of the clan and covered his dead with stones. Yet their ideas of survival after death were vague, drawn mostly from dreams.
63.b17.t: Sontad — born almost two years after the flight
Nineteen children, almost fifty grandchildren, six great-grandchildren
Four adjoining rock shelters, or semicaves
Both killed in an earthquake at forty-two
The family held together until the twentieth generation
63.b19.p: The Andonites had black eyes and a swarthy complexion, and melanin, the pigment found in all human skin, is the original Andonic skin pigment. In appearance they were most like the present-day Eskimo, and they were the first to use animal skins against the cold. They were very imitative, but their play instinct was weak; they smiled now and then but never laughed heartily. Humor was the legacy of the later Adamic race.
63.b20.p: The men fought heroically for their families, and the women were devoted to their children, but their loyalty stopped at the immediate clan; they could not grasp the idea of making the world better for their grandchildren. Altruism was not yet born, although all the emotions needed for the birth of religion were already present. The sight of a warrior fighting with one hand while protecting a wounded comrade foreshadowed the noblest traits of later man.
63.b21.t: What they did not yet have
Courage and devotion for their families
The idea of a better world for their grandchildren
The later sensitivity to pain and unpleasantness
63.b22.p: The Andonic clans built a well-developed language, adding to it almost daily, and it remained the tongue of Urantia until the colored races appeared. But in the twenty-seventh generation, when Sontad’s direct line had no male heir, rivals fought for leadership, and the clans became absorbed in hunting and revenge. In the wars that followed, some of the most valuable strains were forever lost. This is why the Life Carriers provide for the eventual separation of mankind into distinct races.
63.b24.p: The Andonites did not go far into Asia or into Africa; they moved north until the third glacier stopped them. Before the ice reached France and the British Isles, they had spread west over Europe and founded more than one thousand settlements. Much evidence of them remains along the river Somme, whose course the glaciers never changed.
63.b25.p: They lived under overhanging cliffs along the rivers and in hillside grottoes, where they could enjoy their fires without much trouble from smoke; they built dome-shaped stone huts and closed them at night by rolling a large stone across the entrance. As Andon had invented the stone ax, his descendants discovered the throwing stick and the harpoon. A tool-creating mind was at last working together with an implement-using hand. They showed an intelligence their retrogressing descendants did not reach again in half a million years.
63.b27.p: As the dispersion widened, the culture and spirituality of the clans declined for nearly ten thousand years. Then Onagar took the lead, brought peace among the tribes, and for the first time led them all in the worship of the “⟦Q 63:6.1⟧Breath Giver to men and animals.⟦/Q⟧”
63.b28.p: Before that, Andon’s beliefs had been confused. He nearly became a fire worshiper, reasoned his way to the sun but found it too remote, feared the elements, and through hunger drifted toward animal worship. The custom of not eating a venerated animal and holding ceremonies around its body was the origin of sacrifice in worship, an idea that passed through Moses to Paul’s doctrine of atonement by “⟦Q 63:6.4|4:5.4|4:5.5⟧the shedding of blood.⟦/Q⟧”
63.b29.t: Nearly worshiped for the comfort it gave
A greater source, but too remote to worship
Thunder, lightning, rain, snow, hail, and ice were feared
Worshiped as symbols of creative might and sustaining power
The worship of one Deity under Onagar
63.b30.q: “⟦Q 63:6.6⟧O Breath of Life, give us this day our daily food, deliver us from the curse of the ice, save us from our forest enemies, and with mercy receive us into the Great Beyond.⟦/Q⟧”
63.b31.p: From his headquarters at Oban, near the present Caspian Sea, Onagar sent out teachers to spread the doctrine of one Deity and the Great Beyond. They were the world’s first missionaries and the first human beings to cook meat with fire. Born 983,323 years ago, he lived sixty-nine years and set up an efficient tribal government not equaled for many millenniums. It was in his days that the Adjusters and guardian seraphim came to Urantia in great numbers; this was truly the golden age of primitive man.
63.b32.h: 7. The Survival of Andon and Fonta
63.b33.p: Andon and Fonta were recognized at the adjudication held when the Planetary Prince arrived, and they passed through the mansion worlds to become citizens of Jerusem. They have never returned to Urantia, but they know the history of their race. They grieved over the Caligastia betrayal and sorrowed at the Adamic failure, but rejoiced greatly when they heard that Michael had chosen their world for his final bestowal.
63.b34.p: On Jerusem both were fused with their Thought Adjusters, as were several of their children, including Sontad, though most of their immediate descendants achieved only Spirit fusion. Today they serve on the first mansion world, welcoming the pilgrims of time from Urantia. They asked to send greetings to Urantia along with these revelations, but the request was wisely denied.
63.b35.t: Recognized when the Planetary Prince arrived
Became citizens of Jerusem after the mansion worlds
Fused with their Thought Adjusters on Jerusem
Welcoming new pilgrims on the first mansion world
63.b37.p: Paper 63 tells the beginning of mankind through the life of one couple. Two children who held each other on a stormy night and set out together discovered fire, raised nineteen children, and died together. Their descendants scattered and declined through warfare, yet through Onagar they learned again of one God and the Great Beyond. And for Andon and Fonta death was not the end: fused with their Adjusters, they now welcome the pilgrims who follow them on the first mansion world. The path walked by mankind’s first parents shows ahead of time the road of eternal survival that all of us are to travel.
63.b38.t: The parents of all mankind sensed, through personality and the Adjusters, that they were more than animals
Flight in spite of fear and the discovery of fire opened the way to independence
Nineteen children and a strong clan spirit made the first human family
The emotions of religion were present, but clan wars lost precious strains
Spreading across Europe before the ice, they became toolmakers
The golden age of primitive man, taught of one God and the Great Beyond

The first parents, fused with their Adjusters, now welcome pilgrims
63.b40.box: Mankind’s first parents held on to each other and set out in fear, reached eternal survival at last, and walked ahead of us on the road we are to travel.
